RC10.2 repairs first-task context selection in newly installed projects and makes JEV failures
actionable. Before the first Git commit, the added-file inventory no longer pins every bootstrap
instruction ahead of the project evidence. Mandatory guidance, explicit paths and task declarations
retain priority. Generated `_local` output is excluded from automatic context discovery.

JEV receipts retain HTTP status with fixed billing, authentication, request-rejection and overload
reasons, without retaining arbitrary response bodies or credentials. Passive decision doctor separates
configuration eligibility from observed current-configuration inference and labels shadow answers.
Context doctor reports local knowledge and skill paths outside approved disclosure. It never widens
sharing. New projects must explicitly approve newly authored areas they intend JEV to assess.

Ordinary `context-route` now returns selected evidence, original references, omissions and compact
status. Use `context-route --json` for the full diagnostic format; programmatic packets and native
replay retain their existing contracts. Explicit external-read telemetry verifies the source Git
workspace, relative path and digest without disclosing external content to JEV.

A dedicated installed greenfield suite is required by package publication. It exercises installation
with no initial commit, native-format prompt entry, first-task evidence, binding, replay, disclosure
repair, missing-token fallback, billing denial, recovery, ordinary checks and cleanup. Offline
inference is a deterministic fixture. A separate `test:greenfield -- <archive> --live` path requires
a funded JEV account and synthetic source only. Account funding remains an external prerequisite;
offline proof does not establish live provider readiness, native host trust or token savings.

Upgrade deliberately at a pause seam in each execution worktree. This release does not change
adopter disclosure policy, refill provider credit or update sibling pins automatically.
